title: [Developer, real English gameplay, 14s] AXIOMA — fixed AI-assisted art and readable scientific combos
author: Typical-Instance-376
selftext:
For AXIOMA, I used generative AI to assist the scientific illustrations, scientist portraits, felt textures, card-pack art, text and translations. These are fixed assets included in the game, not live generation during a run.



The design question here is legibility: the artwork shares the screen with formula names, card terms and a chips × multiplier score. This is a 14-second clip of actual gameplay with the English interface, showing two scientific formulas combine into 90 × 3 = 270 points.



Can you follow the two formulas before the score resolves, or does the card artwork compete with the information you need? I would be interested in which part of the visual hierarchy is hardest to read.



My game is available for Windows on Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5308770/AXIOMA/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5308770/AXIOMA/)



Samuel Isidoro — developer, Quanta.
